finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. Any authenticated user can therefore wipe any tenant without holding the OWNER role.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. The caller controls the tenant path parameter and does not need the OWNER role.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive operation on tenant data

trace.note: requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role); the javadoc says it does not throw
the boolean result is ignored as a bare statement

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is requireRole at line 26, and its result is unused. checkRole, which throws, is used in export() but not in wipe(). There is no other authorization check, and no tenant-membership check on the path.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 (returns boolean, never throws, result discarded); no other check. The throwing checkRole is only used in export() at line 32.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which only returns a boolean (lines 14-15) and never throws, and discards the result, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated caller; no other file references wipe or Admin, so nothing else guards it.
